overview: Qatar is a small country on a peninsula in the Persian Gulf, bordering Saudi Arabia. Its capital and largest city is Doha. Qatar became independent from British protection in 1971 and is ruled by an emir. Its huge reserves of natural gas have made it one of the richest countries in the world, and in 2022 it hosted the football World Cup.

geography.text: Qatar is a low, flat peninsula of desert and gravel plains, with sand dunes in the south-east around Khor Al Adaid, the 'Inland Sea', a tidal bay surrounded by dunes. Summers are extremely hot, there are no rivers, and most of its water comes from desalinating seawater.

history.text: Qatar was a centre of pearl diving and has been ruled by the Al Thani family since the mid-1800s. It became a British protectorate in 1916, found oil in 1939 and became independent in 1971. Huge offshore gas reserves, found in the 1970s, made it one of the richest countries in the world, and it hosted the 2022 football World Cup.

events.title: Al Thani rule
events.text: Britain recognises the Al Thani family as Qatar's rulers.

events.title: British protectorate
events.text: Qatar signs a protection treaty with Britain.

events.title: World Cup
events.text: Qatar hosts the first World Cup in the Middle East.

government.text: Qatar is an absolute monarchy ruled by the Emir from the Al Thani family. Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani has been Emir since 2013. A Consultative Council advises the government. Qatar has played a big role as a mediator in conflicts in the region.

economy.text: Qatar has huge reserves of natural gas and is one of the world's biggest exporters of liquefied natural gas. That makes it one of the richest countries in the world per person. It also owns Qatar Airways and the Al Jazeera news network.

culture.text: Qatar's traditions come from Bedouin desert life and the sea: falconry, pearl diving and dhow sailing. Its capital, Doha, has grown rapidly into a city of skyscrapers and museums, such as the Museum of Islamic Art. Most residents are foreign workers.

items.title: Falconry
items.text: A desert tradition listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Museum of Islamic Art
items.text: Designed by architect I. M. Pei, opened in 2008.

sport.text: Qatar hosted the 2022 football World Cup, the first in the Middle East, and won the Asian Cup in 2019 and 2023. Mutaz Essa Barshim shared Olympic high jump gold in 2021.

items.title: Mutaz Essa Barshim
items.text: Shared Olympic high jump gold in 2021.

didYouKnow: Qatar has one of the highest incomes per person in the world.
Qatar was the smallest country ever to host a men's football World Cup, in 2022.
